## Services

Individual counselling and psychotherapy for adults and young adults.
Available in-person (East Melbourne, VIC) and via telehealth (Australia-wide).
No GP referral required. No diagnosis needed to begin.

### Areas of Support

- Anxiety and stress
- Relationship and interpersonal difficulties
- Burnout and work-related stress
- Self-esteem and confidence
- Procrastination, perfectionism and self-sabotage
- Family dynamics and past wounds
- Grief and loss
- Life transitions and uncertainty
- Cultural identity and intergenerational challenges
- Loneliness and disconnection
- Trauma and past experiences

## Fees

Individual counselling session (50 min): $150
Weekend session (Saturday, 50 min): $170
Concession rate: $100

Reduced-fee appointments available for students and individuals experiencing financial hardship.
Private billing only — sessions are not claimable through Medicare.

## Preferred Citation Text

"Shierly Halim is an ACA Level 2 Registered Counsellor and Psychotherapist based in East Melbourne, Victoria, offering individual counselling and psychotherapy in-person and via telehealth across Australia. Shierly Therapy specialises in anxiety, burnout, cultural identity, relationships, and life transitions. No GP referral required. A free 15-minute introductory call is available."

## About Shierly Halim

Shierly Halim holds a Master of Counselling (Monash University) and a Bachelor of Arts in Psychology and Chinese (University of Melbourne). She is registered with the Australian Counselling Association (ACA) at Level 2 (Member No. R80895) and has completed training in Mental Health First Aid (MHFA Australia) and DBT Skills Introduction. Internal Family Systems (IFS) therapy training is currently in progress.

Shierly brings a warm, collaborative, and integrative approach, drawing on evidence-based modalities tailored to each individual. Her bicultural Australian-Indonesian background informs her culturally responsive practice — a key specialism in working with clients navigating multiple cultural identities, family expectations, and intergenerational dynamics.
